# vue-snap — full reference

> Lightweight (~5KB) Vue 3 carousel built on native CSS Scroll Snap. ESM-only, ships TypeScript declarations, SSR-safe (Nuxt works out of the box).

Package: `vue-snap` · License: MIT · Repo: https://github.com/bartdominiak/vue-snap

## Installation

```
npm install vue-snap   # or: bun add / pnpm add / yarn add
```

Peer dependency: `vue ^3.5`.

## Usage — local import (recommended)

```vue
<script setup>
import { Carousel, Slide } from 'vue-snap'
import 'vue-snap/style.css'
</script>

<template>
  <Carousel>
    <Slide v-for="item in items" :key="item.id">{{ item.title }}</Slide>
  </Carousel>
</template>
```

## Usage — global plugin

```js
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import VueSnap from 'vue-snap'
import 'vue-snap/style.css'

createApp(App).use(VueSnap).mount('#app')
// Registers <Carousel> and <Slide> globally
```

## Carousel — props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `tag` | String | `'ul'` | HTML tag used for the slide container |
| `hideArrows` | Boolean | `false` | Hides both navigation arrows entirely |
| `hideArrowsOnBound` | Boolean | `false` | Hides the relevant arrow when the first/last slide is active |
| `autoplay` | Boolean | `false` | Automatically advances slides, looping back to the start |
| `autoplayInterval` | Number | `3000` | Delay in milliseconds between autoplay advances |
| `i18n` | Object | `{ slideLeft, slideRight }` | Accessible labels for the built-in arrow buttons |

Hovering the carousel pauses autoplay; it resumes on mouse leave.

## Carousel — events

| Event | Payload | Fires when |
|-------|---------|------------|
| `mounted` | Boolean | The carousel has mounted |
| `slide-change` | Number | The active slide changes (payload = new index) |
| `left-bound` | Boolean | The first slide becomes active |
| `right-bound` | Boolean | The last slide becomes active |
| `autoplay` | Boolean | Autoplay pauses (`false`) or resumes (`true`) |

## Carousel — slots

| Slot | Props | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `default` | – | Slide content, typically `<Slide>` items |
| `arrows` | `{ changeSlide, isBoundLeft, isBoundRight }` | Replace the default arrow buttons |

## Carousel — template ref (exposed)

| Member | Signature | Description |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| `goToSlide` | `(index: number) => void` | Scrolls to the slide at the given index |
| `changeSlide` | `(direction: 1 \| -1) => void` | Moves forward (1) or backward (-1) one slide |
| `isBoundLeft` | `boolean` | True while the first slide is active (since 2.1.0) |
| `isBoundRight` | `boolean` | True while the last slide is active (since 2.1.0) |

```vue
<script setup>
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue'
import { Carousel, Slide } from 'vue-snap'
import 'vue-snap/style.css'

const carousel = useTemplateRef('carousel')
</script>

<template>
  <Carousel ref="carousel">
    <Slide v-for="item in items" :key="item.id">{{ item.title }}</Slide>
  </Carousel>
  <button :disabled="carousel?.isBoundLeft" @click="carousel.changeSlide(-1)">Prev</button>
  <button :disabled="carousel?.isBoundRight" @click="carousel.changeSlide(1)">Next</button>
</template>
```

## Slide — props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `tag` | String | `'li'` | HTML tag rendered for the slide element |

## Styling

All styling hooks are plain CSS classes. Slide width (and how many slides are visible) is controlled with flex-basis:

```css
/* 1 slide on mobile, 3 from 768px */
.my-carousel .vs-carousel__slide {
  flex: 0 0 100%;
}
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .my-carousel .vs-carousel__slide {
    flex: 0 0 33.33%;
  }
}

/* Wrapper height */
.my-carousel .vs-carousel__wrapper {
  height: 200px;
}

/* Arrow buttons */
.my-carousel .vs-carousel__arrows { /* base */ }
.my-carousel .vs-carousel__arrows--left { /* left */ }
.my-carousel .vs-carousel__arrows--right { /* right */ }
```

Class reference: `.vs-carousel` (root), `.vs-carousel__wrapper` (scroll container), `.vs-carousel__slide`, `.vs-carousel__arrows` with `--left` / `--right` modifiers.

## SSR / Nuxt

No special setup — DOM access is guarded internally. See the runnable Nuxt example: https://github.com/bartdominiak/vue-snap/tree/main/examples/nuxt-app

## Browser support

All evergreen browsers (native CSS Scroll Snap). Smooth programmatic scrolling requires Safari 15.4+; older Safari falls back to instant scrolling. No polyfills shipped or required.

## Constraints and gotchas

- v2.x is ESM-only: no `require()`, no UMD/IIFE CDN build (last version with those: 1.4.0)
- `left-bound` / `right-bound` emit when a bound is reached (edge-triggered)
- Bound state and the active index update ~100ms after scrolling settles (debounced scroll handler)
- Custom navigation should use the exposed `isBoundLeft` / `isBoundRight` to disable controls at the edges
